#### Composing a target instead of naming one

`--compose-client <id-or-name>` builds an execution stack
for this run instead of\nnaming a saved environment, refined by `--compose-model`,\n`--compose-server-group` and `--compose-secret
`. The stack becomes an unnamed,\ncontent-addressed environment (the same one `environments ensure-adhoc`\nproduces), so composing

the same stack twice reuses one environment.
`--compose-host` is the deprecated spelling of the same flag.

`--wait` it exits
**4** (see the exit-code table above). A per-target failure\ndoes not abort its siblings, so exiting 0 would let a pipeline read \

"1 of 3
runs never started" as a clean launch.

#### `--file`: upload and run a suite file

`eval run --file` reads the vers
ioned suite file (`schemaVersion: \"1\"`),\nauthenticates, then validates. A contract-invalid file exits **2** after the\nauth req
uest; it does not start a run. `eval validate` on the same bytes\nstill exits 1: that command is a verdict on the file; this one i

s not.

The file's `suite.id` is the declared suite identity. The first run creates a
file-owned suite stamped with that id; la
ter runs of the same id in the same\nproject update that suite rather than creating a second one. A UI-authored\nsuite has no decl
ared id, so no file can claim it. Resolve is never by name.\n\nFile `passThreshold` is a fraction; the hosted suite grades on a pe
rcent. The\nconversion refuses rather than approximates. A file count above **10**\n(`repetitions` in a `schemaVersion: \"1\"` fil

e, `iterations` in `"2"`) is
refused by name (`REPETITIONS_CAP`) and is not clamped.

**Which vocabulary the sync speaks is t
he deployment's call.** Before writing\nanything, the CLI reads `GET /capabilities` once. A deployment that advertises\n`vocabular
y.version: 2` gets every request with `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary: 2`\nand case bodies spelled canonically: `iterations` (the exact
count),\n`legacyIterations` (the legacy floor, the same number) and `assertions`\ninstead of `repetitions` / `iterations` / `check
s`. A deployment without the\ncapability block, or without the capabilities route at all, is spoken to in\nvocabulary 1, byte-for-
byte as before. Nothing in the file changes either way:\nthe dialect of the file and the vocabulary of the wire are independent.\n
\nCases are synced in batches of at most 100 (`create_eval_cases`). Every\ndeclared case is created or updated, including `disable
d: true` rows. A case\nthe file **no longer declares** is deleted from the hosted suite before\nlaunch. A case the file still decl
ares but marks `disabled: true` is **kept,\nwith its history**; it is simply left out of the launch, so parking a flaky\ntest does
not destroy its past results and re-enabling it later resumes the\nsame case.\nThe run is scoped to the enabled cases either way.
A file with no enabled\ncases is refused (`NO_ENABLED_CASES`) rather than launching the whole\npersisted suite. `--case` may only
name an enabled case. A later run updates\nexisting cases by declared id and creates new ones. An enabled case that\noverrides `p
assThreshold` is refused: hosted grading is suite-wide. A\ndisabled case with the same override is ignored, matching how repetitio

ns
are checked. Authored
`defaults.toolPolicy` and non-empty `defaults.validity` gates are refused at
hosted CLI launch (`TOOL_
POLICY_UNSUPPORTED` / the corresponding validity\nrefusal). Hosted platform-authored suites do not currently have a\ntool-policy f
ield or enforcement path, so the CLI does not upload a suite that\nwould claim those guarantees. When supported by an eval runner,
`toolPolicy`\nis enforced at execution time with denied tools kept visible but blocked;\nserver annotations are advisory and **UN
TRUSTED**. The file's default count\n(`defaults.repetitions`, or `defaults.iterations` in `schemaVersion: \"2\"`) is\ninherited pe
r case and is not uploaded as a suite `minIterations` floor.\nAuthored `defaults.systemPrompt` and `defaults.temperature` are uplo
aded as\nexecution defaults; omitted fields stay omitted so the platform applies its\nown defaults. `target.hosts` and `target.env
ironment` are attached before\nlaunch. A file environment takes precedence over file hosts for that launch,\nwhile an explicit CLI
target takes precedence over both. When an explicit CLI\ntarget is provided (for example `--host`), the file's `target.hosts` are
\n**not** synchronized to the suite's persisted host attachments; the suite\nkeeps whatever hosts it already has. Host attachment
synchronization only\nruns when no explicit CLI target overrides the file. Environment attachment\nsynchronization is unaffected a

nd always runs.

Without `--idempotency-key`, the CLI mints a fresh UUID for every invocation
and prints it to stderr before la
unch (`Eval idempotency key: <key>`). Each\ninvocation therefore starts and bills a new run. To retry a launch whose\nresponse was
lost (without starting a second run), pass the key that was\nprinted: `--idempotency-key <printed-key>`. A replay is marked `dedu

ped` in
the receipt and human output. `--notes` is not part of the key.

##### Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-ru

n approval

Every file run performs the same live check `eval validate --project` performs,
**before it writes anything**. It i
s not opt-in and there is no flag to skip\nit. A file with no deterministic `toolCall` steps asks no question and pays no\nround t

rip.

What happens when a deterministic reference does not resolve depends on the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| Sel
ected (enabled, and named by `--case` if you used it) | The launch **refuses before the suite is synced**: nothing is written and
nothing is billed |\n| Imported, not selected | Its claim is rewritten to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **still
persisted**, so the hosted record says what MCPJam found rather than still asserting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native, no
t selected | Left exactly as authored. A hand-written case never acquires an `import` block from this: \"somebody wrote this\" and
\"something converted this\" are different facts |\n\nEach target is checked on **its own** server set. `--host` is checked again
st\nthat host's configured servers rather than the file's, because that is the set\nthe run connects: validating `target.servers`
would approve a tool the host\ncannot reach. A host the FILE declares uses its own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (those are
attached to the host before launch) and the host's\nconfigured set when the field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers: []`\n
is a real, empty set (it clears the attachment before launch) and is\nvalidated as such, never as an omitted field. A step that pi
enumerated before the suite exists\n(`--all-targets`, `--compose-*`), or a host does not report a server set, or a\nhost pins a se

rver the project no longer has, the launch refuses rather than
assuming the references are fine.

`--case` accepts a hosted row
id, which does not exist yet when this check\nruns. A selector this stage cannot map is therefore treated as possibly naming\nany

enabled case, so an unresolved reference still refuses; the launcher
resolves the selector itself a moment later.

A selected

`approximated` case refuses unless this invocation approves it:

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--allow-ap
proximated <case...>` | No | Approve an `approximated` imported case for **this run only**, by AUTHORED case id (`cases[].id`). Re
peatable. `--file` runs only |\n| `--approval-reason <text>` | With the above | Why the approximations are acceptable for this run
. 1–500 characters after trimming; one reason covers every approval in the invocation |\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variable
s\"}\nmcpjam cloud eval run --file .mcpjam/evals/s_billing.yaml \\\n --allow-approximated c_refund_partial \\\n --approval-reaso

n "Reviewed against the upstream rubric; ENG-4821"
```

Checked before anything is billed, each with its own message: approvi
